issues.description: Method: Rideable.messageOnRide. The problem statement (UML and textual description) declares a no-argument method messageOnRide() returning String and the template Main.java calls r.messageOnRide() with no arguments. In contrast, the solution repository declares Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) and the implementing classes Pig and Seal implement messageOnRide(int speed) and return strings that include the speed. This parameter-list mismatch (no-arg vs. one int parameter) will cause compilation errors or test mismatches depending on which signature is used and prevents students from implementing the method consistently.
issues.suggestedFix: Choose one consistent signature and apply it across all artifacts. Option A (align with problem statement and template): change the solution to define Rideable.messageOnRide() : String (no parameters) and update Pig and Seal to implement messageOnRide() returning "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]" (remove speed usage). Update solution Rideable.java, Pig.java, and Seal.java accordingly. Option B (preserve solution intent): update the problem statement UML/text and the template Main.java examples to declare and call messageOnRide(int speed) and update the expected return format in the description to include the speed (e.g., "Riding on [Animal Type] [name] at [speed] mph"). Apply the chosen change to all three locations (problem statement, template code, and solution) so signatures match exactly.

issues.description: The exercise requires a Rideable method messageOnRide() with no parameters that returns a String in the format "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]" (problem statement and template). The solution repository instead defines Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) and implements messageOnRide(int speed) in Pig and Seal, changing the method signature (adds an int parameter) and the return text (adds " at X mph"). The template Main calls r.messageOnRide() with no argument. This mismatch between the problem statement/template (no-arg method) and the solution (method with an int parameter) will confuse students about which signature to implement and how to call the method.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix: change the solution to match the problem/template by replacing Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) with messageOnRide() (no parameters) and update Pig and Seal to implement public String messageOnRide() that returns exactly "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]" (use getClass().getSimpleName() or hardcode the type string and getName()). Alternatively, if the speed parameter is intentional, update the problem statement, UML, and template Main to declare and call messageOnRide(int speed) and document the expected return format (e.g. "Riding on [Animal Type] [name] at [speed] mph").
